html:
Jyotirao Phule was a reformer from Pune who attacked the caste system from below and opened schools for girls and for the lowest castes. Later anti-caste movements start with him.

He was born in 1827 into the Mali caste of gardeners; his family supplied flowers to the old court. He went to a Scottish mission school. In 1848 he was thrown out of a Brahmin friend's wedding procession because of his caste, and he dated his life's work from that day.

That year he and his wife Savitribai, whom he had taught to read, opened a school for girls in Pune, one of the first run by Indians. His father turned them out of the house for it. More schools followed, for girls and for the Mahar and Mang castes then called untouchable. They ran a home where widows could give birth safely, and in 1868 they opened the well of their own house to untouchables.

In 1873 he founded the Satyashodhak Samaj, the society of seekers of truth, which held weddings without Brahmin priests. The same year he published Gulamgiri, "Slavery". It argues that the Brahmins had enslaved the lower castes, and he dedicated it to the Americans who had ended slavery.

Ambedkar named Phule as one of his three teachers.
